scope: Three generated Idaho areas and two established references assessed for Jezero regional-terrain reconnaissance. Area identities and literature precede stronger claims.
selectionRule: Review the original high-scoring sample 04, the next generated candidate 09, and sample 06 as a documented volcanic example, alongside Craters of the Moon and same-pipeline Amboy controls. Retain failures and adverse findings.

literature.title: Black Butte–Magic Reservoir regional sample
literature.finding: USGS identifies the Black Butte basaltic lava field at 43.18° N, 114.35° W inside this area. Low-shield and lava-pit research already discusses this region in planetary context. The area also contains the BLM Magic Reservoir reference point.
literature.boundary: The source vent and reservoir marker lie inside the analysis bounds. Lava-unit and reservoir polygons have not been digitized here.
literature.novelty: Prior planetary research is documented. A new coordinate or terrain score does not establish a newly discovered analog.

sources.title: USGS — Black Butte Crater Lava Field
De Crescenzo et al. (2022), LPSC 2944 — Black Butte lava pits

proposedExercise.basis: Project inference from regional terrain measurements
proposedExercise.question: How would the terrain differences between Jezero Crater and Idaho sample 4 (43.250, -114.240) change a regional observation plan?
actions: Use the existing slope and elevation views to select observation areas spanning the terrain ranges present.
Record coordinates, supporting measurements and the reason for each proposed observation in the notebook.
Reconsider the plan using the footprint-sensitivity results and list the finer data needed for follow-up.

literature.title: Western INL–Atomic City regional sample
literature.finding: USGS table 4 places the West of Atomic City Vent (43.449, −112.844) and Lavatoo Butte (43.531, −113.094) inside this area. These support local basaltic geological context. The table coordinates use NAD83 and are used here for approximate regional containment.
literature.boundary: Mapped vent locations establish point context. They do not identify the rock type of every cell or supply a mapped experimental footprint. Land ownership and access across the area require separate assessment.
literature.novelty: A bounded search did not establish prior use of this exact 32 km footprint as a Jezero regional-terrain analog. Novelty remains unverified. The landforms are already documented geologically.

sources.title: USGS SIR 2025-5020, table 4 — basalt vents near INL

literature.title: Rock Corral Butte regional sample
literature.finding: The published Rock Corral Butte vent coordinate, 43°22.25′ N, 113°1.20′ W, lies inside this area. The cited study examines basaltic flow inflation and its implications for small volcanic shields on Mars and Venus.
literature.boundary: Containment applies to the published vent point. The full 7 × 11 km flow footprint and individual deposits have not been intersected with this DEM area.
literature.novelty: Planetary-analogy literature already exists for this landform. Its regional Jezero terrain index is a separate project comparison.

sources.title: Hottendorf et al. (2023), LPSC 2644 — Rock Corral Butte
